I am 58 years old. I never went to school. Everything I know about farming I learned from my mother and from doing it myself for 40 years. I have 9 mu of land in Quzhou County. My family has 7 people — my son and daughter-in-law work in factories in the city and send money home, which helps me buy inputs, but I am the one who decides what happens on the land.

My main field is 6 mu of wheat-maize, one after another. For winter wheat, I use improved seed from the dealer in town. I buy the same kind that Wang Laohan bought last year, his wheat was very good. At planting time, each mu gets half a bag of compound fertilizer in the furrow. When the wheat turns green in spring, I spread one small bag of urea on each mu. I irrigate three times: once before winter if the soil is dry, once when the wheat starts jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide twice. Last year I got about 1000 jin per mu, this year should be the same.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed the same day we cut the wheat. Summer is short, I don't plough, I plant straight into the wheat stubble so I don't lose days. Each mu gets some compound fertilizer in the hole at planting, and when the maize is knee-high I spread urea. Two irrigations — one when it tassels, one in August if the rain doesn't come. Two pesticide sprays. In busy times like harvest and planting on the same day, I hire two workers from the village to help. Should get about 1100 jin per mu.

My 2 mu of cotton is on the south side. I plough it deep in spring. I use improved seed. Cotton needs more care and more medicine. I put compound fertilizer when planting, then urea when it flowers, and more when the bolls are growing. Three irrigations. Four pesticide sprays because the bollworm is bad every year. I expect about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu.

On the corner near the well, I plant 1 mu of mungbean. I keep my own seed, the traditional kind my family has saved for years. Mungbean doesn't need much — a handful of compound fertilizer at planting, one irrigation, one spray for aphids. I get about 200 jin per mu.

I have to think about my whole budget. If I spend too much on one thing, I have less for another. But I would rather cut somewhere else than cut fertilizer on my wheat and maize. Two years ago my neighbor tried to save money on fertilizer and his wheat was short and yellow. I will not make that mistake. A bad harvest means my grandson cannot pay for school. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost; losing the crop is a disaster. I watch what my neighbors do, and I do about the same. If it worked last year, I will do it again.
